coordinateNote: Coordinates verified against official venue pages, Tabelog, the GSI address-search API, and the saved-place export. Floor and building data added from official sources. Some pins are address-level approximations. Check opening hours and reservations directly with each bar.

bars.name: Apollo Bar Ginza
bars.address: B1F MEIKO Building, 8-2-15 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: I went down to this basement alone and ended up spending hours with the bartender on samurai films, whiskey, and music. By now he's an old friend: a man who loves old movies and, as far as I'm concerned, a modern-day samurai. The room is dim and New York in style, the tonic is house-made, and the whiskey shelf is worth the trip by itself. Expect a ¥1,000 cover and very little English. It's a bar you walk into alone, and it doesn't leave you that way.

bars.name: Star Bar Ginza
bars.address: B1F MODERNS GINZA, 1-5-13 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: Down a flight of stairs in Ginza, Hisashi Kishi hand-cuts each cube until it's nearly transparent, and the Sidecar is what people come for. He was the first Japanese bartender to win the IBA world cocktail title and the government calls him a master craftsman, but the room doesn't trade on that. Hushed, low-lit, and it works for one person at the counter as well as a celebration. ¥1,100 table charge, plan on ¥6,000 or more. Open 5:00 to 11:30 nightly.

bars.name: Lamp Bar
bars.address: 4F Wakamatsu Building, 6-6-19 Ginza, Chuo-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: The name says lamp, but think rum. About three hundred bottles behind the counter, plus cigars, up on the fourth floor of the Wakamatsu Building. The bar moved here from Ginza 4-chome, and it still feels like a neighborhood spot that ended up in the wrong neighborhood: relaxed, easy, more regular than tourist. Open until 2:00, closed Sundays and holidays. Budget at least ¥5,000.

bars.name: New York Bar
bars.address: Park Hyatt Tokyo, 52F, 3-7-1-2 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Odakyu / Keio), 10 min walk
bars.description: The Park Hyatt spent nineteen months renovating, reopened in December 2025, and had the sense to leave this bar alone: same fifty-second floor, same windows, same live jazz, with better acoustics and a cocktail list that nods to Lost in Translation, the film where two strangers meet at this bar. Cocktails start at ¥2,000. The ¥2,500 jazz cover begins with the music, so arrive between 5:00 and 6:30 if you'd rather not pay it. Go early on a weeknight for a window seat.

bars.name: Bar Cocktailbook Shinjuku
aliases: バー カクテルブック 新宿
bars.address: 2F Plaza Nishishinjuku, 7-5-5 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Odakyu / Keio), 5 min walk
bars.description: Akira holds cocktail competition titles, put in twelve years at a Shinjuku hotel bar, and opened this second-floor room in 2011. The menu follows the season and changes monthly, and some of his originals never got names. When I ordered, he set a small pour of each spirit next to the drink so I could taste them on their own first. Thirteen seats, ¥600 charge, closed Sundays and Mondays, near Seibu-Shinjuku.

bars.name: KAKURETAI
bars.address: B1F Nakabayashi Building, 1-2 Arakicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: An unmarked basement in Arakicho with a cheese-and-mouse theme running through the décor, J-pop on the speakers, and Yuta behind the bar. He makes seasonal fruit cocktails and pours Japanese whiskey, and treats first-timers like they've been coming for years. It's openly LGBTQ+ friendly. Weeknights only, 8:00 to 1:00, with DJs on Fridays. It's small and fills up, so reserve.

bars.name: Bar rest
bars.address: 3F Dai-san Hirasawa Building, 2-46-7 Kabukicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Odakyu / Keio), 5 min walk
bars.description: I couldn't find a single independent review, only the bar's own description, so consider this a lead. Third floor, a minute from Seibu-Shinjuku. Seven counter seats line the window and look straight onto the Seibu and JR tracks, where a train passes about once a minute until the last one, and then the maintenance cars come out. Take the window if you came alone; the box seat holds six if you didn't. No food, smoking allowed, Tuesday to Saturday until midnight.

bars.name: a BAR Sleeping Tales
aliases: ア バー スリーピング テイルズ
bars.address: B1F (right door) Towa Shinjuku Gyoen Co-op II, 2-1-14 Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: There's no menu. Toshi asks what you like, checks what's in season, and makes you something. The peanut-butter Old Fashioned is the one that gets brought up. The room is a basement done up like medieval Europe, with vintage glassware and only counter seats, so you watch him work the whole time. Right-hand door at B1F, near Shinjuku Gyoemmae Station. Closed Wednesdays.

bars.name: Golden Gai: Happy, BAR COO & OPEN BOOK
aliases: ハッピー ロッキンソールバー
bars.address: 1-1-6 to 1-1-8 Kabukicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Shinjuku (JR / Tokyo Metro / Toei), 5 min walk
bars.description: Three bars in Shinjuku Golden Gai, the dense cluster of 200-plus tiny drinking dens off Kabukicho. Pick any of the three, or bar-hop between them. Happy is up on the 3rd floor of the Maruha Building, a soul-and-rock counter with a wall of vinyl. BAR COO is at street level on the third lane, five or six seats with Miya behind the counter in fluent English. OPEN BOOK is on the fifth lane, no signboard, just a wooden board that slides open. A lemon sour bar.

subvenues.name: Happy (Rockin' Soul Bar)
subvenues.description: Climb to the third floor of the Maruha Building for rock and soul from the sixties through the eighties, played at full volume, with a wall of vinyl you're welcome to pick from. The cover is about ¥900, there are more than a hundred bottles, and the last Friday of each month is disco night.

subvenues.name: BAR COO
subvenues.description: Five or six seats at street level on Golden Gai's third lane, with Miya running things in fluent English. Snacks are whatever she's made: miso soup, seaweed salad, a slice of Gouda. You end up talking with regulars and other travelers, which makes it a good bar to walk into alone. Get there early. Closed Sundays.

subvenues.name: OPEN BOOK
subvenues.description: No signboard, just a wooden board that slides open on Golden Gai's fifth lane. You come for the lemon sour: brown-sugar shochu, house lime syrup, Hiroshima lemons, big ice. The books on the shelves belonged to the owner's grandfather, the Naoki Prize-winning novelist Tanaka Komimasa. About fifteen people fit, mostly standing, and it's always full. ¥300 charge, 8:00 to midnight.

bars.name: JANAI COFFEE
bars.address: B1F Yamanen Building, 2-3-13 Ebisuminami, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Ebisu (JR Yamanote / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 3 min walk
bars.description: Getting in is the gimmick. You solve a puzzle on their website to reach the booking page, reservations are online only, and the door at the bottom of the stairs is a bookcase. Inside, coffee cocktails and craft cocktails cost ¥1,400 to ¥1,600, or ¥3,500 for three. The staff speak English, the playlist is R&B, and you leave with a cup of decaf. It works as well solo as it does with a group. Open 6:00 to midnight.

bars.name: A10
bars.address: B1F Bios Building, 1-12-11 Ebisunishi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Ebisu (JR Yamanote / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 3 min walk
bars.description: Walk past what looks like a row of green lockers and you're in a record bar. A DJ on vinyl, soul and jazz on a serious sound system, and original cocktails overseen by Munenori Nagumo. ¥1,320 charge. Open 7:00 to 2:30. Book ahead for Fridays and weekends.

bars.name: Never Never Land
aliases: ネヴァーネヴァーランド
下北沢ネバーネバーランド
bars.address: 2F Yoshino Heights, 3-19-3 Kitazawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo 155-0031
bars.description: A Shimokitazawa rock bar open since 1978, up on the second floor across from Studio Noah, three minutes from the station. The walls are covered in posters and fliers for gigs and underground theater, and there are DJ nights and live sets. The kitchen does spiced Asian food; the Burmese chicken curry is the one to order, at ¥1,300. No cover charge, about twenty-four seats, non-smoking, solo diners welcome. Expect ¥2,000 to ¥3,000. Open 6:00 to 1:00, with irregular days off.

bars.name: No Room For Squares
aliases: ノー・ルーム・フォー・スクエアーズ
bars.address: 4F Housing Kitazawa Building II, 2-1-7 Kitazawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: Named after the Hank Mobley album. It's on a fourth floor in Shimokitazawa, and you enter through the front of an old Coca-Cola vending machine. More than a thousand records, huge speakers on the walls, and no menu; tell the owner what you like. Weekends bring live jazz, and during a set the room is too small for conversation. A good bar to walk into nervous. Cash only, 2:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m.

bars.name: Bar sawa
bars.address: 1F Forum Nakameguro, 1-6-7 Higashiyama, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: Shigeko Shintani opened this Nakameguro whiskey bar in 1985 and has visited more than 130 distilleries since. Behind the counter are over eight hundred whiskeys, including bottles like a Dalmore Sirius and a 1948 Macallan. Open every night until 5:00 a.m., with half-price drinks from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m. You will probably spend more than you meant to. Look for the yellow light over the door.

bars.name: Gen Yamamoto
bars.address: 1F Anniversary Building, 1-6-4 Azabujuban, Minato-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: One bartender, eight seats, and a tasting course of small cocktails built from seasonal Japanese produce that changes almost every week. Plan on ¥8,000 to ¥10,000. The pours are small and the alcohol is light; the flavors make up for it. Book by phone up to a week ahead. Tuesday to Saturday, last entry 9:00, so this is an early-evening stop, not a late one.

bars.name: Bar Centifolia
aliases: バー センティフォリア
bars.address: 6F La Muse Azabujuban Building, 1-6-5 Azabujuban, Minato-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: Yuzo Komai makes cocktails as a performance. Some of it is art, some of it is Instagram hype. The menu is fixed, with no classics and no substitutions. Drinks run about ¥4,000 each, plus a ¥1,000 charge and tax. Not a place to get drunk. Fourteen seats, open until 3:00.

bars.name: BAR &UNDER
aliases: バー アンドアンダー
bars.address: B1F Sotokanda Kanemura Building, 2-6-4 Sotokanda, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Akihabara (JR / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 5 min walk
bars.description: A basement bar in Sotokanda, about seven minutes from Akihabara. Koji Yamamoto quit TV production to tend bar and has since come up with more than two hundred sake cocktails, many based on characters, plus collaboration nights with anime and YouTubers every couple of weeks. He says the ampersand in the name means doing something together. About thirty seats, a young crowd, board games, a ¥700 seat charge, and a one-drink minimum; the whole idea is to make bars less intimidating for newcomers. Closes at 11:00, closed Mondays.

bars.name: NARU Jazz Livehouse
bars.address: B1 Jujiya Building, 2-1 Kanda Surugadai, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 101-0062
bars.station: Ochanomizu (JR Chuo/Sobu, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 1 min walk
bars.description: Open since 1969, a minute from Ochanomizu Station. About thirty seats crowded around a grand piano, working Tokyo musicians every night, a ¥2,500 cover plus drinks, and generous food that doesn't cost much, most of it Italian. English menu. It's tight in there, and that's what makes it intimate. Solo or with a group, you get a good welcome.

bars.name: Game Bar A-Button
aliases: ゲームバー エーボタン
bars.address: 1F Dai-5 Mitsumasa Building, 1-13-9 Taito, Taito-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: Don't come to play games; the owner pulled most of the playable machines after copyright letters. What's left is a thirteen-seat bar in an old ramen shop packed with consoles, controllers, and figures, run by Nagamine, a former Sega arcade worker. It's a gathering spot for people who love this stuff. Drinks are on the expensive side and English is limited. Open until 11:00.

bars.name: BAR Willow's
bars.address: 6F-E, 88 Building, 2-1-3 Ueno, Taito-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Okachimachi (JR), 3 min walk; Ueno-Hirokoji (Tokyo Metro Ginza), 1 min walk
bars.description: I don't visit Tokyo without coming here, usually several times a trip. Yanagisawa owns the bar, ran the bar at the Yokohama Royal Park Hotel before this, and is about as attentive as a bartender gets; his English is excellent. The ice is hand-crafted and priced like it, and that is what good service costs. Each chair at the counter was chosen by hand, and the chair in the logo means there's always a seat waiting for you. After enough trips, there is. Two hundred whiskeys, good non-alcoholic drinks, open until 3:00 most nights.

bars.name: Rock Bar Sakebi
aliases: ロックバー さけび
bars.address: 1F, 2-16-11 Negishi, Taito-ku, Tokyo
bars.description: Sakebi means scream. The room is nearly pitch dark, lit by a few odd lights, with ten counter seats and a sound system that stands out. The owner mixes rock with jazz, blues, and techno. Drinks are cheap, snacks run a couple hundred yen, you can smoke, and you can't reserve. It's comfortable for drinking alone. Five minutes from the north exit of Uguisudani Station. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

bars.name: Eigakan Jazz
bars.address: B1F, 5-33-19 Hakusan, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo 112-0001
bars.station: Hakusan (Toei Mita Line A3), 1 min walk
bars.description: Eigakan means cinema. Yoshida-san, a former film director, opened this jazz kissa in 1978, a minute from Hakusan Station and down a flight of stairs. The sound is clear and full without being loud, and the room is for listening. About twenty seats, cash only, smoking allowed, no reservations. Tuesday to Saturday, 4:00 to 10:00.

bars.name: SAKEBARO Aoyama
bars.imageAlt: Sake and wine bottles behind two metal sake cups and a small dish of almonds on the SAKEBARO counter
bars.address: 1F MD Aoyama, 2-10-8 Minami-Aoyama, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0062
bars.description: Members only, with screening to get in. Inside are a tin-cube counter, a tin piano that plays itself, LED walls that move from blue to red, and staff who can give you the brewery, yeast, and polish rate of every pour. Conversation stays hushed. Now and then there's a ticketed dinner for non-members; book online and they email you the address. You can walk into everything else in this guide. Not this one.
bars.note: Reservation or membership required. Arrange access well before you travel.

bars.name: Rokusan Angel (Burlesque Tokyo)
bars.address: B2F Roppongi Nittaku Building, 3-8-15 Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo
bars.station: Roppongi (Toei Oedo / Tokyo Metro Hibiya), 5 min walk
bars.description: Formerly Burlesque Tokyo, two floors below street level in Roppongi. The themed shows change every week and run seventy to ninety minutes, and the performers work the crowd. It's booked for birthdays and celebrations, so bring people, and reserve early for front seats. Expect ¥8,000 to ¥10,000 each after the 15% service charge. Limited English.
